solvers.syllabus_ref: 4.1 outliers (1.5 IQR); 4.2 freq tables, cum freq, median, quartiles, percentiles, IQR, box plot values; 4.3 mean, mode, grouped mean (mid-interval), sd and variance
steps: Box: min {mn}, Q1 {Q1}, med {med}, Q3 {Q3}, max {mx}
ANS: mean={mean}, median={med}, Q1={Q1}, Q3={Q3}, IQR={IQR}, sd={sd_3sf}
solvers.python_logic: AREA HELPERS (pure Python, shared by all stats solvers): num(s)=float(G('evalf('+s+')')); ex(s)=G('simplify('+s+')'); sf3(v) formats a float to 3 s.f. with bounded scaling loops (no '%g' trailing-zero loss, e.g. 0.120); z4(v) 4 d.p. for z-values; isdec(list) True if any input contains '.', then answers shown as decimals (exact if terminating, else 3 s.f.), otherwise exact + (3 s.f.). Every G() inside try/except -> out('Error: '+what); return. THIS SOLVER: parse with split_top(s,','). Sorting uses python floats (fv=[num(t)]) with sorted(range(n), key=fv index) while keeping original strings for exact display. Quartiles use the TI/IB 'median of halves' rule: h=n//2, lower=positions 1..h, upper=positions n-h+1..n (median excluded when n odd). For freq tables do NOT expand: kth(k) walks the cumulative frequency list (bounded by number of values) to return the k-th ordered value; median/quartile positions computed as above. Mode: dict count (raw) or max f (freq), all ties printed. Outliers: compare float values with fences; whiskers = min/max of non-outliers. Grouped: mids m_i=(b_i+b_{i+1})/2, cumulative list, class containing target t=n/2, n/4, 3n/4, p*n/100 found by bounded loop, linear interpolation, labelled (est). Variance via the computational formula with exact strings through dot(); sd printed as expression then 3 s.f. (technology quantity). Long lists printed 8 per line through out().
solvers.scope_limits: Population sd sigma_n only (IB convention); sample s_(n-1) not shown. Raw lists up to ~200 values (string length/memory); grouped quartiles/percentiles are interpolation estimates, not graph readings. Non-numeric entries or mismatched x/f lengths -> 'Error: list lengths' and return. If G fails on long sums, fall back to python float sums and print 3 s.f. only.

inputs: 1 aX+b  2 unknown from mean  3 combine groups  4 add/remove value [1]
solvers.python_logic: Sub-menu via ask(). [1] if only sd given -> var=G('(sd)^2'); if only var -> sd=G('sqrt(var)'); print 'sd unchanged' line instead of formula when a=1. [2] Unknown symbol = first alphabetic token in x or f strings that is not a function name (sqrt, ln, exp, sin, cos, tan, e, pi); exactly one allowed. Build Sfx='x1*f1+...'; Sf='f1+...'; print both via normal(); show cleared equation normal(Sfx - mean*Sf)=0; solve; parse_list; if unknown is a frequency keep non-negative integer roots only (else print all roots and 'check'). [3]/[4] straight formula lines. Uses area helpers ex/sf3/isdec.
solvers.scope_limits: One unknown in [2]; two unknowns need a second condition -> message 'Use Discrete RV / 2 eq' and return. Transformations are linear only (aX+b). If solve returns [] -> 'No solution: check data'.

solvers.syllabus_ref: 4.4 Pearson r, regression line y on x, use for prediction, interpret a and b; 4.10 regression line x on y
steps: Sxy = Sum xy - n xbar ybar = {Sxy}
[y on x] a = ybar - b xbar = {a}
[x on y] c = xbar - d ybar = {c}
[interpret] b: y changes by {b_3sf} per unit increase in x
[interpret] a: value of y when x = 0
solvers.python_logic: split_top lists; require equal length n>=3 else error. All sums exact through dot() so integer data give exact r (e.g. sqrt(15)/5) before 3 s.f. Strength label from |r| (>=0.75 strong, >=0.5 moderate, else weak; r=0 'no linear correlation') printed as one line only. Prediction uses the unrounded a,b (or c,d for x from y, per 4.10 rule: predict x from y with x on y line). Extrapolation flag by comparing float x0 with min/max of the data. Interpretation lines only if asked (student rule: no unsolicited explanation).
solvers.scope_limits: Linear regression only (non-linear/exponential models are AI, not AA). Sxx=0 or Syy=0 -> 'Error: no variation'. Lists over ~40 points may overflow the command string -> fall back to python float sums and print 3 s.f. values.

solvers.syllabus_ref: 4.5 complementary events, expected occurrences; 4.6 Venn, P(AuB)=P(A)+P(B)-P(AnB), mutually exclusive, conditional, independence; 4.11 formal conditional P(A|B)=P(AnB)/P(B), test P(AnB)=P(A)P(B)
inputs: 1 two events  2 regions with x  3 two-way table [1]
steps: [1 per rule fired] P(AuB) = P(A) + P(B) - P(AnB)
solvers.python_logic: [1] Variables a,b,c,u,g,h,w; blank -> unknown; user values may contain a symbol x (treated as unknown). Decimal inputs are converted with exact() so arithmetic is exact; display uses isdec rule. Rules R1 u=a+b-c, R2 g*b=c, R3 h*a=c, R4 w=1-u, R5 c=a*b (if indep), R6 c=0 (if mut.excl). Phase 1: bounded loop (max 6 passes): for each rule, if exactly one of its variables is unknown, print the rule formula and the substituted line, G solve for that variable, keep roots in [0,1], mark known. Phase 2: if unknowns remain, print 'Solve simultaneously:' with all rules containing unknowns, one G('solve([...],[...])'), keep solution sets whose values lie in [0,1]. Then derived lines (complements, Venn regions). Independence/ME tests printed only when relation not given and a,b,c known; equality decided by G('simplify(c-a*b)')=='0'. Consistency check: c<=min(a,b), u>=max(a,b), all in [0,1], else 'Inconsistent data'. [2] regions list (supports 3-set Venn), solve sum=T, then wanted/given conditional by index lists. [3] up to 3x3 counts; row/col totals in python, fractions via simplify.
solvers.scope_limits: Two events in mode [1] (three events handled only as region lists in [2]). One symbolic unknown per value. If both phase 1 and phase 2 fail -> 'Not enough information'. Non-probability values (outside [0,1]) rejected.

solvers.syllabus_ref: 4.6 tree diagrams, combined events; AHL 4.13 Bayes theorem (up to 3 events), total probability
inputs: Known P(Ai|B) to solve for x (blank):
solvers.python_logic: m in {2,3}; bounded for i in range(m). Missing last prior auto = 1 - sum of others (printed). Validate priors sum to 1 via simplify(sum-1)=='0' else 'Priors must sum to 1'. Branch products, total probability, then requested Bayes quotient. If any input contains x and a known posterior is given, form the equation ri/PB = given, solve, keep roots in [0,1], then recompute PB with x substituted. Display per isdec rule (exact fraction + 3 s.f., or decimals).

solvers.syllabus_ref: 4.5 complement ('at least one'); 4.6 successive events with and without replacement, tree diagrams
inputs: Event 1 sequence 2 exactly k 3 at least 1 4 all same 5 at least k [1]
solvers.python_logic: c colours (<=4), d draws (<=4) so at most 4^4=256 sequences. Enumerate with a single bounded loop idx in range(c**d), digits obtained by repeated %c and //c (no recursion). For each sequence copy counts, build the product string 'a/b*...' (decrement count and total when no replacement), test the event predicate, and store in a dict keyed by (numerator,denominator) python ints -> list of sequences. Print up to 6 matching sequences with their products; if all matches share one product print 'count x product' (mark-scheme form). 'At least 1' always printed by complement. 'At least k' groups exactly-j totals for j=k..d. Final sums simplified by G normal().
solvers.scope_limits: <=4 colours, <=4 draws. Larger draws -> print the combination ratio C(..)C(..)/C(..) via comb() (without replacement) or redirect to Binomial (with replacement). Draw-until-first-success over unbounded trials not supported.

solvers.syllabus_ref: 4.7 discrete random variables, sum of probabilities = 1, E(X), fair games; AHL 4.14 Var(X), E(aX+b), Var(aX+b)
solvers.python_logic: Lists <=12 values. Unknowns = alphabetic tokens (excluding sqrt, ln, exp, e, pi, trig names) found in P strings (and in x strings for fair games); 0, 1 or 2 allowed. 1 unknown in P: sum=1, solve, then validity filter loop over roots: every substituted P must satisfy 0<=P<=1 (evalf); print rejected roots. 2 unknowns: need Extra=1 (E given) -> solve system. Unknown in x values with Extra=2 -> E=0 equation (fair game). After substitution compute E, E(X^2), Var, sd. Query: parse operator (>=,<=,>,<,=) and number, select xi by float comparison, sum the matching P. Optional aX+b lines. Display per isdec rule.
solvers.scope_limits: Finite support only (<=12 values); infinite discrete distributions are not in AA. Binomial questions -> Binomial solver. If no root is valid -> 'No valid k'. More than 2 unknowns -> 'Too many unknowns' and return.

solvers.syllabus_ref: 4.8 binomial distribution B(n,p): P(X=r), cumulative probabilities, mean np, variance np(1-p); 4.5 expected number of occurrences; finding n or p
inputs: 1 P(X=r) 2 P(X<=r) 3 P(X<r) 4 P(X>=r) 5 P(X>r) 6 P(a<=X<=b) 7 mean/var 8 least n 9 find p [1]
solvers.python_logic: q=simplify(1-p). Cumulative values computed exactly as a finite sum with sum() then evalf (binomial_cdf only as fallback, UNVERIFIED). Write the probability statement first, the cumulative identity (complement / shift of r) second, then the 3 s.f. value; the r<=2 case also shows individual terms. Exact answer shown when p is a fraction and the query is P(X=r) (e.g. 3/8). [8] k=1: logarithm inequality with sign reversal noted by printing the flipped inequality, then ceil. k>=2: bounded search n from k to 1000 using python float pmf recurrence (pmf(i+1)=pmf(i)*(n-i)/(i+1)*p/q) to find the first N; then confirm N-1 and N with G and print both lines. [9] solve, keep roots with 0<p<1 (evalf), print all valid roots. Expected occurrences (4.5) = mode 7 mean line.
solvers.scope_limits: n<=1000 (cumulative via sum may be slow on device; fallback python float sum printed to 3 s.f.). p must be in [0,1]; r integer in [0,n] else error. Normal approximation and Poisson are not in AA and not offered.

solvers.syllabus_ref: 4.9 normal distribution probabilities and inverse normal; 4.12 standardisation z=(x-mu)/sigma; conditional probability with normal; chaining to binomial
inputs: 1 P(X<b) 2 P(X>a) 3 P(a<X<b) 4 P(X<x)=p 5 P(X>x)=p 6 P(mu-c<X<mu+c)=p 7 conditional [1]
Use result as p in B(n,p)? n (0=no) [0]
solvers.python_logic: Probabilities via normald_cdf (UNVERIFIED); on G failure use the erf formula (established). One-sided: blank/inf bound -> cdf or 1-cdf. Keep all intermediates at full precision (pass G strings, not rounded floats); print z to 4 d.p. (or GDC-style notation normCdf/invNorm as the expression line), final 3 s.f. Inverse: P(X>x)=p converted to lower tail 1-p; symmetric case uses (1+p)/2. invNorm via normald_icdf (UNVERIFIED) -> fallback fsolve on erf (UNVERIFIED syntax) -> final fallback bounded python bisection on [-8,8], 45 iterations, each evaluating G('evalf(erf(..))'). Conditional: python intersects the two intervals (None = infinity); empty intersection -> P=0. P(X=a) for a single value prints 'P(X={a}) = 0'. Chain option passes the unrounded probability string to binomial_dist.
solvers.scope_limits: sigma>0 and 0<p<1 required, else error. No continuity correction / normal approximation to binomial (not AA). Results are technology values: printed expression then 3 s.f.

solvers.syllabus_ref: 4.12 standardisation; finding unknown mean and/or standard deviation from given probabilities (simultaneous equations with inverse normal z-values)
solvers.python_logic: Convert each condition to a lower-tail probability pl (type 2: 1-p; type 3: 1/2-p, with x below mu). z from normald_icdf (UNVERIFIED) with the same fallbacks as normal_prob. Single unknown: rearrange the standardisation line explicitly. Both: print equations (1),(2), the subtraction line, then linsolve for verification; keep z at full precision; reject solution with sigma<=0 ('check inequality directions'). p=0.5 with sigma unknown -> z=0 -> 'Cannot find sigma from p=0.5'.
solvers.scope_limits: Two conditions maximum; relations like mu=2sigma or conditions involving both variables nonlinearly -> fallback: print the two standardised equations and solve with G solve, flagged '(GDC)'. Non-normal models out of scope.

solvers.syllabus_ref: AHL 4.14 continuous random variables, pdf incl. piecewise: find k from integral=1, P(a<X<b), mode, median, E(X), E(X^2), Var(X), E(aX+b), Var(aX+b)
inputs: Extra cond e.g. E=2 or f(1)=0 (blank):
Tasks 1 k 2 P 3 E,Var 4 median 5 mode 6 aX+b 0 all [0]
steps: ANS: k = {k}, E(X) = {E}, Var(X) = {V}, median = {m}, mode = {xm}
solvers.python_logic: Store pieces as list of (f_i, lo_i, hi_i), <=3, contiguous. Each definite integral is shown as antiderivative (G integrate) + bracket evaluation via subst at both bounds + simplify, so the working is visible; if the integrand is a product needing by parts (e.g. x*e^(-x)), print 'by parts' and reuse the calculus area's IBP routine if present, else show the antiderivative. Unknowns: one -> solve integral=1, keep root making f>=0 (sampled at 5 points per piece with evalf); two -> also form the extra equation (E(X)=v via x f integral, or a pdf value/continuity at a breakpoint) and solve the system. P(c<X<d): bounded loop over pieces, integrate on [max(c,lo),min(d,hi)] where non-empty. Median: cumulative c_i over pieces in order (bounded), first piece where cumulative >= 1/2, equation with c_prev; solve for m, parse_list, keep root with lo<=evalf(root)<=hi; if solve returns none valid, fsolve with guess=(lo+hi)/2 and label (GDC). Mode: per piece roots of f' within (lo,hi) plus all endpoints/breakpoints, evaluate f, pick max; for interior max print f'' check. aX+b from E and Var. Upper bound 'inf' handled with limit(F,x,inf).
solvers.scope_limits: <=3 pieces, <=2 unknowns; cumulative distribution function as a function is not required in the 2021 AA guide and not output. f must be non-negative on its domain (warning printed otherwise). Median equations of degree >4 or transcendental are solved numerically (3 s.f., labelled GDC). Integrals Giac cannot do in closed form -> numeric evalf of the definite integral with '(GDC)'.

tests.input: f=k*x^2 on [0,3], all tasks, P(1<X<2), a,b=2,1

not_automatable: 4.1 Sampling concepts (population vs sample, random/systematic/stratified/quota/convenience sampling, bias, reliability of data sources): qualitative definitions and judgement, nothing to compute.
4.1 Deciding whether an outlier should be removed or is a data error: needs judgement about the context. The solver only flags values beyond 1.5 IQR.
4.2 Drawing histograms, box plots and cumulative frequency curves, and reading values off a printed graph: graphical work. The solver gives the numbers to plot and interpolated estimates instead.

4.3/4.4 Comparing or commenting on distributions, judging whether a linear model suits a scatter diagram, correlation versus causation, interpreting results in context: written reasoning. Only the short a/b interpretation templates are printed, and only when asked.
4.5/4.6 Drawing Venn diagrams, tree diagrams and sample-space diagrams: visual. The solver outputs region values and branch products in text form.
4.7/4.8 Choosing a distribution and stating modelling assumptions (independent trials, constant p, fixed n; or why a normal model fits): word answers that depend on the context.
4.11/4.13 Algebraic 'show that' proofs of probability identities or deriving Bayes' theorem: proofs, not calculations. Numeric checks such as the independence test are automated.

4.14 General proofs, e.g. proving E(aX+b)=aE(X)+b or showing a parametric function is a pdf for all parameter values: proof-style. The solver only checks the given case (integral = 1, f >= 0 at sampled points).
4.9 Sketching and shading normal curves, and symmetry arguments given in words: graphical. The probabilities themselves are computed.
unverified_giac: normald_cdf(mu,sigma,x): argument order and whether it returns lower-tail P(X<x). Also the 4-argument interval form normald_cdf(mu,sigma,a,b). Fallback: (1+erf((x-mu)/(sigma*sqrt(2))))/2
normald_icdf(mu,sigma,p): name and argument order. Fallback: fsolve on erf, then Python bisection
binomial_cdf(n,p,r): name, argument order, and whether r is inclusive. Only used as a fallback; the primary method is sum(comb(n,i)*p^i*(1-p)^(n-i),i,0,r)
exact(0.3): converting a float to a rational (3/10) in the KhiCAS build
fsolve(eq,var=guess): syntax and that it returns a single float in KhiCAS. The interval form fsolve(eq,var=a..b) is also unverified
erf(x): assumed present in the KhiCAS build (needed for every normal fallback)
solve(...) output format in KhiCAS: possible 'list[...]' wrapper, how real cube roots are given (e.g. 3*2^(2/3)/2), and whether real-only mode drops complex roots. parse_list must handle these
limit(F,x,inf): whether infinity is spelled 'inf' or '+infinity' in KhiCAS
integrate(f,x) on piecewise-free expressions with parameters k,a: assumed to treat k and a as constants without assume()
MicroPython math.erf: may be missing on the Ndless build. The bisection fallback must call G('evalf(erf(..))') instead
